title: Travis Kelce helped lead the Chiefs to a 24-10 win over the Dolphins, then publicly complained that penalties are killing the game's momentum - NewsBreak
text:
By Saif Ur Rehman ,
6 hours ago Image by Erik Drost, CC BY 2.0. Via Wikimedia Commons. Travis Kelce contributed to the Kansas City Chiefs’ win against the Miami Dolphins, but the athlete reportedly had something to say about the refereeing calls during the match. Talking about the flags during the match, Kelce said they disrupt the game’s momentum, which can be challenging for players and teams to manage.
According to HITC, Travis Kelce discussed the game on a podcast with his brother, Jason Kelce. He said these flags waste momentum and can end drives teams have planned. But he didn’t just criticize the referees for those calls; he also said players should keep their fundamentals in check to avoid them. He said these issues are becoming common regardless of the team.
Travis, who was also identified as one of the victims of a $35 million Ponzi scheme, reportedly stated during the New Heights podcast, “A lot of flags on both sides of the ball, for both teams. It puts a halt to the momentum that you’re trying to get. Ends drives. You just gotta try and hone in on those fundamentals and make sure you’re not giving the refs anything to call. That’s just how the game goes.” He added, “14 touchdowns have been erased by penalties so far this season, the fourth most through three weeks since the year 2000.”
Despite the penalty issues, Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce saved the show for the Chiefs The Chiefs stayed ahead with help from Patrick Mahomes at QB. Mahomes, who once joked about snubbing Travis as his top choice for a vacation partner, went on to throw the ball for 246 yards, managing 2 touchdowns in the process. He completed over 80 percent of his passes. Mahomes controlled the game, with Travis making the runs. Kelce caught 2 passes, grabbing 58 yards and scoring a touchdown on one of them.
As for the fouls called in the game, Kansas vs. the Dolphins had 16 fouls in total, with both teams committing 8. For these fouls, the Kansas City Chiefs were penalized 84 yards, while the Dolphins were penalized 64 yards. But the most significant foul in Kansas City’s favor came when edge Chop Robinson was flagged for roughing the passer on third-and-nine while the Chiefs were on their own 5-yard line. That could have turned the game in the third quarter of the game.
Talking about the foul, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley stated, “We had the clear entry to the quarterback,” Hafley said, “I thought he hit him solid square on, and I thought he tried to do his best to raise his hands and get out of the way. But they saw it as a foul, and they called the foul.” So, despite the penalty concern Travis raised on the New Heights podcast, the Chiefs still took the win.
